question: What is the name for the gestures used in Bharatnatyam?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mudras**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mudras** are symbolic hand gestures used in Indian classical dance forms, including Bharatnatyam, to convey specific meanings and emotions.
 
• In Bharatnatyam, mudras are a crucial aspect of the dance and are used to tell a story, depict characters, and express various emotions.
 
• There are two types of mudras in Bharatnatyam: **Asamyukta Mudras** (single-hand gestures) and **Samyukta Mudras** (double-hand gestures).
 
• The use of mudras in Bharatnatyam is codified in the ancient text **Natyashastra**, which provides detailed descriptions of various gestures and their meanings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Laya**

 
 
• Laya refers to the concept of rhythm or tempo in Indian classical music and dance.
 
• It is an essential element that helps in maintaining the timing and synchronization of movements and music.
 
• Laya can be classified into three categories: **Vilambit** (slow tempo), **Madhya** (medium tempo), and **Drut** (fast tempo).
 
• In Bharatnatyam, dancers often perform to different layas, showcasing their skill in maintaining rhythmic precision.
 
 
 
• **Tripatakas**
 
 
• Tripataka is one of the single-hand mudras (Asamyukta Hastas) used in Bharatnatyam.
 
• The Tripataka mudra is formed by holding the thumb, index, and middle fingers straight while bending the ring finger and little finger.
 
• This gesture can represent a crown, a tree, a lamp, or an arrow, depending on its context and accompanying movements.
 
• It is one of the 28 single-hand mudras described in the Natyashastra.
 
 
 
• **Gatakas**
 
 
• Gatakas is not a recognized term in the context of Bharatnatyam or Indian classical dance.
 
• It may be a typographical error or confusion with similar-sounding terms.
 
• In Indian classical dance, specific terminologies are used to denote various gestures, rhythms, and movements, and Gatakas does not fit into this lexicon.
 
• Understanding the correct terms and their meanings is crucial for a deeper appreciation of the dance form.
